why: “In your Shooting phase, you can select one friendly ORKS WALKER unit within 3" of this model. That unit’s attacks can re-roll hit rolls of 1 until the end of the turn.” That covers your Shooting phase and, through “until the end of the turn”, your Fight phase. No core rule gives attacks in the Charge phase. The other bullet, “This model has Lone Operative”, is carried by the ability’s own def line (“Lone Operative while within 3" of a friendly ORKS WALKER unit (not BIG MEK)”), which shows under “When targeted” in their Shooting and Fight phases. The app’s other Lone Operative abilities (Lord of Murder, Da Grand Warlord’s Ladz) also have no phase tag.

“you can select one friendly ORKS WALKER unit within 3" of this model. That unit’s attacks can re-roll hit rolls of 1 until the end of the turn.” No exclusion is added: there is no notSelf, so the Big Mek’s own WALKER unit can be picked, as the text allows. The needs filter leaves out ORKS, but every unit in the Cooking list has Faction: Orks (a list fact), and Try Dat Button! and Crazed Rampage use the same filter. “this turn” = “until the end of the turn”.
“In your Shooting phase, if this unit made an ingress move this turn, this unit’s ranged attacks have +1 to hit rolls.” The condition, scope and phase are the same.

“This unit’s attacks that target a unit that has no models with a T of 7+ have +1 to hit rolls” has no phase limit. The unit attacks in your Shooting phase, in the Fight phase of either turn, and in Fire Overwatch (“End of your opponent’s Movement phase … Your unit shoots using snap shooting”, which excludes only TITANIC; Killa Kans are VEHICLE WALKER). For the owner: snap shooting hits only on “an unmodified hit roll of 6 (irrespective of … any modifiers)” (15.09). The tag only indexes where the ability’s own words apply, which is all of the unit’s attacks.
“When a friendly WARBOSS model is destroyed, if this unit has not been selected to fight this phase, roll one D6 …” names no phase, so it is listed in all five.

The condition (“if this unit has not been selected to fight this phase”), the roll (“On a 3+”, “with +1 to the roll if your unit is riled up”) and the removal (“When this unit has fought, or at the end of the phase (whichever comes first)”) are the same. The def keeps the text’s “this unit” / “your unit” without saying which unit they mean.

Text: “In your Shooting phase or the Fight phase, when a friendly ORKS WALKER unit (excluding TITANIC units) is selected to attack, you can use this ability. If you do, roll either one D6 or two D6 (keep re-rolling duplicate results).” The footnote’s when, “Optional D6”, drops the timing. Mod footnotes show on the weapon tables, which are not limited to a phase, so the bonus would also seem to apply to e.g. Fire Overwatch at the end of the opponent’s Movement phase. The Deff from Above footnote was fixed for the same reason. The note itself is literal.

mod.when: Your Shooting phase or the Fight phase, when selected to attack (optional: one D6 or two D6)
mod.note: 1–2 +1 A · 3–4 +2 S · 5–6 +1 AP (two D6: keep re-rolling duplicate results; one hazard roll when the unit has attacked)

why: WHEN “Fight phase”. EFFECT: “When a model in your unit is destroyed, if your unit has not been selected to fight this phase, roll one D6 … On a 4+, do not remove that model from the battlefield. When your unit has fought, or at the end of the phase (whichever comes first), that model is removed from the battlefield.” The def leaves out the clause “+3 to the result if your unit has ~~DEFF DREAD~~”. That keyword is struck through in the source (Wahapedia prints it that way), and no unit in the Cooking list has DEFF DREAD (a list fact), so the clause changes nothing for the WALKER units this line is shown on.

Verbatim from Wahapedia’s Core Abilities (24) FAQ: “Q:If my unit has the Deadly Demise ability and has an ability that allows it to Fight on Death, how do I resolve this? A: Fight on Death rules are resolved before Deadly Demise abilities, meaning that your unit’s Deadly Demise will resolve after your unit has fought/at the end of the phase and the relevant models have been removed from the battlefield.” Crazed Rampage’s effect has the wording of the app’s Fight On Death rule (05.04.05: “do not remove it from play … until their unit is selected to attack and has attacked, or until the end of the phase”). The WALKER units it targets here have Deadly Demise 1. The note adds no conclusion of the app’s own.

“IMPERIAL KNIGHTS models from your army have the Feel No Pain 6+ ability” has no phase limit. The regain part names “the start of your Command phase”. All five phases.
The Feel No Pain 6+ part has no turn limit, so it applies in either turn.

“each time the bearer’s unit destroys an enemy unit, you gain 1 Bloodshed point” has no phase limit. The unit (pistols, GRENADES) can destroy units in your Shooting phase (shooting, Explosives), in Fire Overwatch (their Movement phase) and in the Fight phase of either turn. It is not MONSTER/VEHICLE, so it can’t use Crushing Impact in the Charge phase. “Each time you make a Blessings of Khorne roll”: at the start of the battle round (indexed under Command, the app’s settled convention for that timing) and through Skulls for the Skull Throne! (Fight phase).

“Each time this model makes a ranged attack that targets the closest eligible target within 18", you can re-roll the Hit roll” has no phase limit. The model makes ranged attacks in your Shooting phase and in Fire Overwatch (their Movement phase); the Forgefiend is VEHICLE WALKER, not TITANIC. For the owner: Snap Shooting (15.09) says “You cannot re-roll hit rolls.” The tag indexes where the ability’s own words apply and does not say which of the two rules wins, so it is not a ruling. Leaving that phase out would itself decide the conflict.

Blessings apply “until the end of the battle round” and act on “charge rolls” (the Charge phase of both turns, through Heroic Intervention), on “Pile-in or Consolidation move” and on “destroyed by a melee attack” / melee weapons (Fight phase). The roll is made “at the start of the battle round”. The rule labels that with at: 'Start of the battle round' and lists it under Command (settled convention).

Each part copies its own source with its own condition. Unbridled Bloodlust: “This unit has +1 to charge rolls.” Battle-lust (the Slaughterbound’s enhancement): “while the Unbridled Bloodlust Blessing of Khorne is active for your army, add 1 to Charge rolls made for the bearer’s unit”. Archslaughterer (on the Lord on Juggernaut): “every Blessing of Khorne is active for this unit until the start of your next turn”. Nothing says the bonuses stack, and the “for your army” condition is kept.

Each Blessing is restated with its own condition. Total Carnage: “roll one D6: on a 4+, do not remove it from play. The destroyed model can fight after the attacking unit has finished making its attacks, and is then removed from play”. Rage-fuelled Invigoration: “it can move up to 6" instead of up to 3"”. Decapitating Strikes: “makes a melee attack that targets an INFANTRY unit”. “All six” = Archslaughterer’s “every Blessing of Khorne” (the table lists six).

“In your Movement phase … Until the end of the turn, its Dark Blessing has the [SUSTAINED HITS D3] ability. Until the end of the turn, it is not eligible to declare a charge.” Dark Blessing is this model’s 24" ranged weapon in the list, so the effects reach your Movement, Shooting and Charge phases.

“In your Command phase, if this unit is unengaged, you can use this ability … This unit must make an ingress move in your next Movement phase (including in your first turn).” Command and Movement, your turn.

Rituals are attempted “at the start of your Shooting phase”. Temporal Surge: “until the end of the turn, that unit is not eligible to declare a charge”, which reaches your Charge phase. The rule’s own turn is “your”.

The ability is selected “In your Command phase” and lasts “until the start of your next Command phase”. Its effects act on Psychic weapons: Range, “add 1 to the Wound roll”, [DEVASTATING WOUNDS]. Those weapons are used in Fire Overwatch (Movement), Shooting, and the Fight phase (Magnus, the Daemon Prince and both Sorcerers have Psychic melee weapons). No unit makes attacks in the Charge phase.

“to take effect until the start of your next Command phase”: the window covers the opponent’s turn, so “either” is right for Fight (Psychic melee weapons, “Each time a THOUSAND SONS model from your army makes an attack with a Psychic weapon”) and for their Movement phase (Fire Overwatch). Selection happens only “In your Command phase”, and the three effects only act when Psychic weapons attack. With no per-phase turns, the rule is also listed in their Command phase, your Movement phase and their Shooting phase, where none of your units attacks. This is the brief’s ‘includes one where it can’t’. The fix needs the same per-phase turns key the app’s other attack rules use (Try Dat Button! turns:{shooting:'your'}, Da Hunt is On turns:{movement:'opp', shooting:'your'}). The turn value itself stays “either”.
All three abilities name “THOUSAND SONS models from your army” / “a THOUSAND SONS model from your army”. No PSYKER condition is added.
TARGET: “That THOUSAND SONS model.” No PSYKER condition is added.
“While a friendly TYRANIDS unit is within 9" of this model, that unit is within your army’s Synapse Range.” The condition and the effect are the same. Kind “all” adds no melee-only reading.
“While a friendly TYRANIDS unit is within 6" of this model, ranged weapons equipped by models in that unit have the [ASSAULT] and [LETHAL HITS] abilities.”

“Until the end of the battle, each time this model makes an attack that targets that unit you can re-roll …” and “while this model is within range of that objective marker, it has the Feel No Pain 5+ ability and an Objective Control characteristic of 15”: neither has a phase or turn limit.

“While a TYRANIDS unit from your army is within Synapse Range of your army: Each time that unit takes a Battle-shock test, take that test on 3D6 instead of 2D6.” No phase or turn limit. The text is shortened with the same condition.

“while a TYRANIDS MONSTER unit from your army (excluding Battle-shocked units) is at its Starting Strength, add 2 to the Objective Control characteristic” has no phase limit, and neither does the attack part.

The choice (“any or all”) is kept, and kind ranged matches “ranged weapons”.

One or more of its other ranged weapons.” 10.06 Close-quarters shooting: “Non-MONSTER/Non-VEHICLE Models: You can only select [CLOSE-QUARTERS] weapons to make attacks with”. The sentence ‘Can shoot with A or B, not both (Close-quarters)’ drops 24.07’s condition “When using another shooting type”, so it still offers B in close-quarters shooting, where B can’t be selected. This was point (3) of the earlier audit. The rewrite fixed the ‘all’ wording but not this. Everything else matches: “You can select one or more ranged weapons that model has” (‘can shoot with one or both / one or more of these’), the MONSTER/VEHICLE exclusion, “You must select one melee weapon”, and 24.11 “All of that model’s [EXTRA ATTACKS] weapons. One of that model’s other melee weapons, if possible.” Latent, no change needed today: `big` tests the unit’s keywords, but 24.07 says “each model … (excluding MONSTER/VEHICLE models)” and 19.03 says “models in an attached unit do not gain the keywords of other models”. No attached unit in the five lists mixes MONSTER/VEHICLE and other models, and the data has no per-model keywords.

The new summary, “Every model can shoot with one or more of its guns”, is 04.01 (“You can select one or more ranged weapons that model has”). It is used only when every per-model sentence is the plain ‘Can shoot with one or both / one or more of these’ form. The rest is list facts: which models line carries which weapons, the one-model carrier names, ×N counts, and leader vs bodyguard lines (19.04). The one rule problem sits in useSentence (see that item).
